(i) the AOT is underestimated in the Sahel and overestimated over the Bodélé depression, and (ii) the AOT diurnal cycle is significantly underestimated over the Sahel due to the combination of the diurnal bias in the satellite data and the diurnal bias of the cloud cover in the model.
the AOT diurnal cycle is underestimated over the Sahel due to cloud masking and that the AOT is overestimated in the early morning due to a lack of observations.
the dust AOT is highly variable in space and time.

the diurnal cycle and the impact of clouds in AOT retrievals.

the diurnal cycle is important and should be considered when using satellite AOT retrievals to study the dust cycle in West Africa.
the AOT climatology is underestimated over West Africa by about 40% due to the diurnal cycle.
the diurnal cycle is important and should not be neglected in the AOT retrieval algorithms.

we show how the diurnal cycle can be used to constrain the bias in satellite retrievals.

a combination of observations and model results is needed to constrain the diurnal cycle and the impact of clouds on the satellite‐derived AOT.
